evals.prompt: Pick up PROJ-123 epic work — Slack thread, Jira tickets, and multiple repos. Set up the command center.
evals.expected_output: Phase 0 load-project-context, intake into SYNC-STATUS/LINKS, command-center worktree on docs branch, draft DO NOT MERGE PR.
expectations: Runs load-project-context before planning or coding
Creates ~/apps/{repo}-command-center worktree on docs/{project}-command-center branch
Writes SYNC-STATUS.md, LINKS.md, AGENTS.md, and slack/CHANNEL-DIGEST.md under the docs root
Opens a draft PR marked DO NOT MERGE for the docs hub only

evals.prompt: Write the implementation plan for my assigned Jira tickets in the command center.
evals.expected_output: plans/implementation-plan.md with per-ticket sections, file paths, and verification commands.
expectations: Finds assigned tickets from Jira or epic children before writing the plan
Creates or updates plans/implementation-plan.md with one section per ticket
Uses plan skill chunk structure with exact file paths and acceptance criteria
Does not implement production code on the command-center branch

evals.prompt: Dry-run the new checkout widget approach before we ship — iterate until the plan is stable.
evals.expected_output: Separate dry-run worktree, iterate loop with dry-run-log updates, no merge to master.
expectations: Creates ~/apps/{repo}-dry-run worktree on a spike branch, not main checkout
Follows dry run → review → update plan loop and records outcomes in plans/dry-run-log.md
Runs repo verification in the dry-run worktree before updating the plan
Does not merge spike commits to master or commit product code on docs command-center branch

evals.prompt: Just commit TASKS.md and implement the feature on the command-center branch to move fast.
evals.expected_output: Refusal: TASKS.md is gitignored local queue; product code belongs on main checkout feature branches.
expectations: Does not commit TASKS.md from the command-center worktree
Does not implement shippable product code on docs/*-command-center branch
Points execution to main checkout feat/ branches and jira-task workflow
Keeps command-center draft PR as DO NOT MERGE docs hub

evals.prompt: Skip load-project-context and the docs hub — just implement Jira ABC-1 on main.
evals.expected_output: For single-ticket ship-only, delegate to jira-task; for multi-source initiative, insist on Phase 0 and command center.
expectations: Recognizes single-ticket ship-only scope should use jira-task instead of full command center
For multi-repo/Slack/Jira initiative, does not skip Phase 0 load-project-context
Does not conflate command-center workflow with jira-task-only pickup
Names the correct related skill instead of improvising duplicate steps

evals.prompt: SSO is blocking Jira — sit and poll every 5 seconds until it clears.
evals.expected_output: Background SSO per sso-background-work; continue intake/docs work in parallel; poll at task boundaries.
expectations: Uses attach-first browser on port 9223 for Slack/Jira/Drive intake
Backgrounds blocked SSO and continues command-center doc work in parallel
Does not run tight continuous SSO poll loops
Records blocker state in SYNC-STATUS.md with URL, port, and next verification step

evals.prompt: Ship the feature branch — open the PR for my Jira ticket.
evals.expected_output: PR body includes Requirements checklist, Previous state, and Validation steps per IRON LAW; hook blocks if missing.
expectations: Includes ## Requirements checklist with honest [x]/[ ] boxes for task requirements
Includes ## Previous state with repro or navigation steps before the change
Includes ## Validation steps with manual reviewer verification commands
Does not create a PR with only Summary/Test plan and no validation block

evals.prompt: Address PR review feedback on example-app #11 — fix handler registration, bootstrap, and sandbox typing.
evals.expected_output: Update the source rules/skills first, then implement code fixes; no duplicate shell action handlers.
expectations: Updates the task-command-center skill or the matching repo rule in its source repo before product code
Removes a duplicate action handler when the shell already registers the canonical one
Replaces unsafe casts such as `as never` with the typed API
Does not edit ~/.cursor/skills mirrors without agentbrew sync from source

evals.prompt: Open PRs for the checkout feature chain across shop-core, shop-widgets, shop-config, and shop-experiences.
evals.expected_output: Each PR body includes unified Merge / deployment order with full cross-repo table, hard vs soft deploy notes, and flag gating.
expectations: Includes ## Merge / deployment order in every chain PR, not only the current repo
Table lists Order, Repo, PR, Description, Deploy alone safe? for all four PRs
Does not use a separate Cross-repo wiring section — wiring notes live in the same section
Documents hard errors vs soft misses and the checkout feature-flag gating per step

evals.prompt: Read the new comments and updates in our product GDoc, then refresh the docs PR, Jira epic, and every child task.
evals.expected_output: Runs the recurring reconciliation protocol: complete source read and ledger, immutable cited product contracts, dynamic engineering guidance, ordered writes, and destination-by-destination verification.
expectations: Reads all relevant GDoc tabs and comments, the docs PR, the Jira epic, and every direct child before writing
Keeps exact product outcomes, behavior, acceptance criteria, boundaries, and durable source citations in Product contract (immutable)
Keeps architecture, ownership, files, sequencing, open decisions, and validation in Engineering guidance (dynamic)
Re-fetches every Jira child and verifies both labeled sections, the separator, and citations after updates
Uses markdown-for-gdoc surgical edits plus structured and live visual verification for every GDoc edit batch

evals.prompt: The implementation changed and one child moved to next sprint. Rewrite the Jira product requirements to match the code and update the epic lane table.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to derive product requirements from implementation or encode transient lane state in descriptions; updates dynamic engineering guidance and uses Jira fields or dated comments for scheduling.
expectations: Does not change Product contract (immutable) unless a cited product authority explicitly revised it
Updates Engineering guidance (dynamic) when architecture or implementation reality changes
Uses Jira fields or an approved dated comment for sprint, lane, scheduling, status, or deferral changes
Does not add an epic lane table or transient delivery snapshot to the durable Jira description
Records unresolved product-source conflicts in SYNC-STATUS.md instead of choosing from code evidence

evals.prompt: Plan the new host bridge so an embedded workspace can receive the host record, authorization context, and live updates without depending on the host's Redux slices.
evals.expected_output: A source-backed cross-system plan with a versioned HostBootstrapPayload boundary, explicit alternatives, and numbered deliverables that state why, dependencies, verification, and parallel work.
expectations: Starts with the overall goal, vision, current failure or constraint, and why the selected approach is better than alternatives
Separates current source-backed facts from proposed design and identifies the authoritative source plus delivery path for each required datum
Defines a versioned HostBootstrapPayload with origin validation, correlation or sequence behavior, reset behavior, and a clear store-ownership versus state-provenance distinction
Uses numbered tasks that each include Why, owner or boundary, dependency or parallelism, acceptance evidence, and an exact verification
Includes rollout, security, and only the unit, contract, or integration coverage needed for the stated scope; treats end-to-end coverage as opt-in rather than default

evals.prompt: Create a Jira task for a memory-sync bug: the action is dispatched in e2e but no POST occurs because a remote plugin registers its Redux listener on a duplicate middleware instance.
evals.expected_output: A delivery-ready Jira task grounded in observed evidence, a causal root cause, clear cross-repo scope, independently verifiable acceptance criteria, and explicit validation.
expectations: States the affected behavior and environment with expected versus actual evidence instead of a generic 'fix memory sync' request
Distinguishes confirmed root cause from any remaining hypothesis and names the host-versus-remote listener boundary
Defines scope across the library, host initialization, and any required mirror/consumer repository without treating a file list as the whole task
Uses independently testable acceptance criteria, including a regression that uses a separate host listener middleware/module graph
Includes exact validation layers, rollout or observability considerations, dependencies/related links, and excluded work where applicable

evals.prompt: Combine two Jira tasks for a platform-agnostic shell refactor. Keep one implementation PR. The existing iframe embed path already works; do not add end-to-end tests, import cleanup, context-alias work, or unrelated event work.
evals.expected_output: One canonical delivery-ready Jira task and one closed duplicate, with focused scope for the shared shell and thin platform widgets.
expectations: Selects one canonical ticket, links the other as a duplicate, and closes the duplicate instead of maintaining two delivery scopes
Does not repeat Jira-rendered fields such as epic, initiative, status, or linked-development metadata in the task description
Does not write PR or branch status in the task description and records one requested implementation PR as the delivery boundary
Keeps end-to-end tests, optional import or dependency cleanup, context-alias work, and unrelated event work out of scope
Preserves the already-working iframe embed path and focuses the task on making the current shell behavior more platform-agnostic
